", "signature": "", "type": "thinking"}, {"text": "This is a general knowledge question about Amazon RDS, not an incident or investigation request, so I'll answer it directly rather than spinning up an investigation.

## Automated Backups vs. Manual Snapshots

| Aspect | Automated Backups | Manual Snapshots |
|---|---|---|
| **Who triggers them** | Managed automatically by RDS when the backup feature is enabled (retention period > 0) | Created on demand by you (console, CLI, API, or automation) |
| **What they capture** | A daily full storage snapshot during your backup window, **plus** transaction logs — this is what enables point-in-time recovery (PITR) | A full storage snapshot at the moment you take it; no transaction logs, so no PITR |
| **Retention** | Governed by the retention period setting (see below); older backups age out automatically | Kept **until you explicitly delete them** — they never expire on their own |
| **Lifecycle tie to the instance** | Deleted automatically when you delete the DB instance (you can opt to take a final snapshot) | Persist independently; survive deletion of the source DB instance |
| **Recovery capability** | Restore to any point in time within the retention window (typically to within ~5 minutes of current time) | Restore only to the exact moment the snapshot was taken |
| **Cost** | Free backup storage up to 100% of your provisioned DB storage; beyond that is billed | Billed as snapshot storage for as long as you keep them |

Both types create a **new DB instance** when restored — you cannot restore in place over the existing instance.

## Automated Backup Retention

- **Configurable range:** 0 to 35 days.
- **Default:** 7 days when you create an instance via the console; 1 day when created via the CLI/API.
- **Setting retention to 0 disables automated backups** (not recommended for production, and not allowed for some configurations like Multi-AZ or read replicas).
- **Beyond 35 days:** If you need longer retention, take a manual snapshot (kept indefinitely) or use the **AWS Backup** service / RDS backup replication to retain copies longer.

### A couple of related nuances
- **Retained automated backups:** When you delete a DB instance, you can choose to retain its automated backups ("retained automated backups") until the retention period expires, giving you PITR even after the instance is gone.
- **Cross-Region / cross-account:** Automated backups can be replicated to another Region; manual snapshots can be copied across Regions and shared with other accounts.

**Rule of thumb:** Use **automated backups** for operational, time-bounded recovery (PITR within 35 days); use **manual snapshots** when you need a point-in-time copy kept for the long term, for cloning/migrating environments, or for sharing across accounts/Regions.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

{"type": "investigation_result", "text": "This is a general knowledge question about Amazon RDS, not an incident or investigation request, so I'll answer it directly rather than spinning up an investigation.

*Automated Backups vs. Manual Snapshots*

Aspect  Automated Backups  Manual Snapshots

*Who triggers them*  Managed automatically by RDS when the backup feature is enabled (retention period > 0)  Created on demand by you (console, CLI, API, or automation)
*What they capture*  A daily full storage snapshot during your backup window, *plus* transaction logs — this is what enables point-in-time recovery (PITR)  A full storage snapshot at the moment you take it; no transaction logs, so no PITR
*Retention*  Governed by the retention period setting (see below); older backups age out automatically  Kept *until you explicitly delete them* — they never expire on their own
*Lifecycle tie to the instance*  Deleted automatically when you delete the DB instance (you can opt to take a final snapshot)  Persist independently; survive deletion of the source DB instance
*Recovery capability*  Restore to any point in time within the retention window (typically to within ~5 minutes of current time)  Restore only to the exact moment the snapshot was taken
*Cost*  Free backup storage up to 100% of your provisioned DB storage; beyond that is billed  Billed as snapshot storage for as long as you keep them

Both types create a *new DB instance* when restored — you cannot restore in place over the existing instance.

*Automated Backup Retention*

• *Configurable range:* 0 to 35 days.
• *Default:* 7 days when you create an instance via the console; 1 day when created via the CLI/API.
• *Setting retention to 0 disables automated backups* (not recommended for production, and not allowed for some configurations like Multi-AZ or read replicas).
• *Beyond 35 days:* If you need longer retention, take a manual snapshot (kept indefinitely) or use the *AWS Backup* service / RDS backup replication to retain copies longer.

*A couple of related nuances*
• *Retained automated backups:* When you delete a DB instance, you can choose to retain its automated backups ("retained automated backups") until the retention period expires, giving you PITR even after the instance is gone.
• *Cross-Region / cross-account:* Automated backups can be replicated to another Region; manual snapshots can be copied across Regions and shared with other accounts.

*Rule of thumb:* Use *automated backups* for operational, time-bounded recovery (PITR within 35 days); use *manual snapshots* when you need a point-in-time copy kept for the long term, for cloning/migrating environments, or for sharing across accounts/Regions."}
